newsitem.title: USA: TI Q1 revs hurt by lower DRAM prices.
newsitem.headline: TI Q1 revs hurt by lower DRAM prices.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said Tuesday that its lower first quarter revenues were mainly due to lower prices on dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips.
The company said revenues from continuing operations in the quarter were $2.26 billion, down 15 percent from the year-ago period's $2.68 billion.
In addition to lower prices for DRAM chips, it cited the absence of revenues from the sale of its mobile computing, custom manufacturing services and printer businesses.
The company said excluding memory, semiconductor revenues were significantly higher than a year earlier.
